name: Soft amber fragrances

lead: Soft amber is a subfamily in the fragrance wheel's amber (formerly oriental) family, associated with incense and amber accords. Perfumes in this style are described as warm, soft and powdery, often with vanilla-like sweetness.
People wear them as part of grooming, to leave a pleasant, memorable scent impression. It is a style choice and not a physical-feature change.

paras: Worn as a cologne or perfume on skin or clothing, often for evenings or cooler weather. Wearers choose among brands by trying samples.
Fragrance ingredients can cause skin irritation or allergy in some people.

angle.text: Soft amber fragrances are chosen as a grooming accessory for a warm, inviting scent profile.

lead: Soft amber is one of four subfamilies of the amber family in Michael Edwards's fragrance wheel, alongside floral amber, amber and woody amber. It is linked in the classification with incense and amber accords.[1]

Before 2010 the family was called oriental, and its 1983 subgroups were soft oriental, oriental and woody oriental; the 2010 revision renamed it amber.[1] Fragrance classifications are rough and overlap between sources.[1]
In appearance terms, scent is part of grooming: the style is used for a warm, soft impression, though no studies on soft amber specifically have been published.

paras: The amber family was named oriental until the 2010 wheel revision. Soft amber is linked to incense and amber, floral amber to orange blossom and sweet spices, amber to resins, and woody amber to sandalwood and patchouli.[1]
